newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Dated Brent offered lower as overhang grows.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Dated Brent offered lower as overhang grows.

text.p: Prices for North Sea Dated Brent cargoes weakened again on Friday with Wall Street trader J.P. Morgan taking a further two cargoes from the paper chains and a U.K. major offering the market lower, traders said.
J.P. Morgan, which kept all three cargoes from Thursday's paper chains, added another two cargoes to its inventory today, taking its tally to seven cargoes in all, they said.

The trader was reported to be taking around one million barrels to the U.S. Gulf. There were also reports that a U.K. major, heard offering Dated Brent at Oct paper -35 cents in late trade, was looking to move barrels transatlantic too.
He said that much of the gains could be attributed to short-covering related to stock building.

"Prior to this new conflict lower crude prices meant that stocks had been allowed to dwindle from around 56 days supply to 47, with many players leaving it late to buy in order to take advantage of any dip in prices," the broker said.

This and the ongoing Iraq/U.S. tension was reflected in firmer paper spreads, with Oct/Nov trading up to +78 cents. Trade for other North Sea grades was thin with few September cargoes left. Two Ekofisk, two Oseberg, one Statfjord and a Gullfaks C cargo were seen left for late September loading.
Activity in the Med was subdued with traders attending an industry function in Rome.
Only one Urals deal was reported on Friday with a major paying Dated Brent -75 cents for a Sept 23-25 loader. This numbers was some five to six cents higher than the last deals.
The West African market was also calm with the market awaiting Nigerian official prices for October.
A rumour that one cargo of Forcados loading in the third decade of October was sold into the Amcap tender could not be confirmed.
